clue.text: He works unsocial hours for the present

definitions.text: He works unsocial hours for the present

parts.words: He works unsocial hours for the present
parts.note: reads like a shift worker on nights in the current era, but describes the night-time delivery of Christmas gifts

explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present' sounds like 'for now'; it means for the gift, delivered overnight on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas does his gift rounds through the night while children sleep.

clue.text: An eagle or a quail maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncertain birdwatcher cannot tell whether the bird is a raptor or a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges QUAIL, set after the A. Aquila is the constellation of the Eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila is Latin for the bird and the name of the constellation known as the Eagle.

clue.text: Could hardly care less — for a colour set?

definitions.meaning: to 'not care twopence' is to be indifferent, so this verb phrase points to the coin of the idiom
Victorian toy-theatre sheets were sold 'penny plain, twopence coloured'

explanation.walkthrough: Neither definition is a noun: the first leans on the idiom 'not care tuppence', the second on the price of a coloured sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopence is the coin of the indifference idiom and the old price of coloured toy-theatre prints.

clue.text: British chief who gave motor law and alternating current to us

parts.note: a motor is a car
an Act of Parliament is a law
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribal leader is credited with handing over cars, legislation and electricity to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: CARACTACUS (Caratacus) was a British chieftain who resisted the Roman conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: He led British tribes against the Roman invasion in the first century AD.

clue.text: Lake go-down

definitions.meaning: a descent, here the way down to the underworld

explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's 'facilis descensus Averno' makes the lake near Naples the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The Campanian crater lake was held by the Romans to be the mouth of Hades, the descent below.

clue.text: Tides that go on to become a different tide

definitions.text: Tides that go on to become a different tide

parts.words: Tides that go on to become a different tide
parts.note: tides here are oceans; add the letters of 'on' to their name and you get a word meaning a time of year, as in Eastertide

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tide' has an old sense of season (Yuletide); the oceans plus ON make that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans are poetically 'the tides', and adding ON makes a time of year, another sense of tide.

clue.text: Curve of the return of a slow ball with a sharp blow

indicators.note: a return comes back the way it went, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a slow high ball
a rap is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: A tennis player describes the arc of a lobbed return smashed back hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow ball' is a lob in tennis or cricket; 'the return of' turns the whole run of four pieces round, so the last piece read becomes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is the curved path a thrown ball follows.

clue.text: One of these organs inspired Bruce presumably

definitions.text: One of these organs inspired Bruce presumably

parts.words: One of these organs inspired Bruce presumably
parts.note: Robert the Bruce took heart from a spider that kept trying to spin its web, so the organs are a spider's silk-making ones

explanation.walkthrough: The legend has Robert the Bruce, the Scottish king, watching a persevering spider; its web came from these organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders draw silk from these glands, and the web of one inspired the Scottish king.

clue.text: 'Intents to settle ?

parts.note: read as 'in tents to settle': to settle in tents is to pitch camp

explanation.walkthrough: 'Intents' splits into 'in tents', which is what settling a camp means.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch camp is to settle down under canvas.

clue.text: Crime's a snip for him — though he only wins "trash"?

definitions.text: Crime's a snip for him — though he only wins "trash"?

parts.words: Crime's a snip for him — though he only wins "trash"?
parts.note: the thief literally snips a purse from its strings, and Iago says 'who steals my purse steals trash'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snip' is easy work and a cut; old thieves cut purses from belts. 'Trash' quotes Othello: 'Who steals my purse steals trash.'
explanation.definitionFit: An old pickpocket cut purses free of their straps to steal them.

clue.text: Hold up the colander again ?

definitions.meaning: putting something through a colander a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as RE-STRAIN, sieve once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to hold up; a colander strains food, so using it again strains it anew.

clue.text: "Ere the ——-cocks say Night is growing gray" (Hardy)

definitions.text: Ere the ——-cocks say Night is growing gray" (Hardy)

parts.words: Ere the ——-cocks say Night is growing gray" (Hardy)
parts.note: a line of Thomas Hardy's verse with one word left out, to be filled in from the farmyard

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the cockerels of the farm building crow at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm cockerels roost in the farm building that stores hay.

clue.text: Intriguing flights'

parts.note: stairs at the rear of a house, the servants' route, give their name to underhand intrigue

explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' looks like 'fascinating'; it means scheming, and 'flights' are flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear service stairs lend their name to secret, underhand dealing.

clue.text: Criterion of a fool

definitions.meaning: the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.definitionFit: A testing stone for gold gives a standard of judgment, and the jester of As You Like It bears the name.

clue.text: Shark strikes ' hard 'when handled

definitions.meaning: a fish with a flattened, T-shaped head
the business end of a hammer delivers the blow when the tool is wielded

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the striking part of a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: The shark is named for its T-shaped head; the hammer's metal end is what strikes.

clue.text: Somewhat persuasive bit of gear with some encyclopedias

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective phrase, read as 'something persuasive', for a noun

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

indicators.note: some of the word is taken, its opening run

explanation.surface: A slightly convincing argument about machine parts found in reference books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ENCY from the start of 'encyclopedias'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogency is the quality of being convincing, the force of an argument.

clue.text: Clothes for gentlemen about to prepare for war

indicators.note: the word for gentlemen goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: gents is short for gentlemen
to arm is to prepare for war

explanation.surface: Uniforms for men about to go off to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the word for gentlemen goes round the word for preparing for war; 'for' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are articles of clothing.

clue.text: She could make a male hop -sent Hercules spinning !

indicators.note: the letters could make a new word, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman could make a man dance and sent the hero Hercules spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A MALE HOP. The queen of Lydia set Hercules to spin wool while he served her.
explanation.definitionFit: Omphale was the Lydian queen whom Hercules served as a slave, spinning wool.

clue.text: State of things that cause our hands to shake

definitions.meaning: a muddle, as in 'a fine kettle of fish'

definitions.text: that cause our hands to shake
definitions.meaning: the old greeting given with a handshake

explanation.definitionFit: A fine mess is called a pretty how-d'ye-do, and the same words greet someone as you shake hands.

clue.text: School.. of painters in.. brown?

definitions.meaning: the art school of a Tuscan city

explanation.walkthrough: Raw and burnt sienna are earth browns named after the Tuscan city of Siena.
explanation.definitionFit: Duccio and Simone Martini led the Tuscan city's school, and its earth gives brown pigment.

clue.text: There is a place for youth in poetry

definitions.text: There is a place for youth in poetry

parts.words: There is a place for youth in poetry
parts.note: A. E. Housman's poem cycle names its young man after an English county

explanation.walkthrough: A Shropshire Lad is Housman's poem cycle; SHROPSHIRE is an English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's poems are titled after a lad from this county.

clue.text: Their end is unthinkable!

parts.note: at the end of these you cannot think straight, as in the idiom for desperation

explanation.walkthrough: At one's wits' end means unable to think what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental faculties are meant; being at their limit is the idiom for desperation.

clue.text: Dicky bird ? Specifically no

parts.note: a small bird, but named Tom rather than Dick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky bird' is nursery talk for any small bird; this one is specifically not a Dick but a Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: The small songbird is a little bird, a child's dicky bird, whose name begins with Tom.

clue.text: A prime minister. North

definitions.meaning: the Earl who led Britain during the Crimean War

explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was also a prime minister, which pulls 'North' towards the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth Earl held the premiership in the 1850s; the granite city lies in Scotland's north.

clue.text: Produce at risk in one consignment

definitions.text: Produce at risk in one consignment

parts.words: Produce at risk in one consignment
parts.note: the proverb warns against putting all of these in one basket

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb: don't put all your eggs in one basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens' produce, proverbially risky to carry in a single basket.

clue.text: They were mixed manfully in Brutus, said Antony

definitions.text: They were mixed manfully in Brutus, said Antony

parts.words: They were mixed manfully in Brutus, said Antony
parts.note: Antony's tribute in Julius Caesar: 'the ... so mixed in him that Nature might stand up and say this was a man'

explanation.walkthrough: From Antony's last speech over Brutus in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The four humours or basic components were so balanced in Brutus that he was the model of a man.

clue.text: Assessing the land-lubber too!

definitions.meaning: a naval rank-and-file sailor, even a raw recruit

explanation.walkthrough: In the Navy an ordinary sailor is a rating, so even a landlubber who joins is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuing something is grading it, and naval seamen below officer rank are so called.

clue.text: They achieve top-knots over, permanent waves

definitions.text: They achieve top-knots over, permanent waves

parts.words: They achieve top-knots over, permanent waves
parts.note: reads as hairdressing, but means reaching top speed in knots over the sea's endless waves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-knots' and 'permanent waves' are hair styles; here they are top speed in knots and the sea's waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast motorboats reach a high number of knots across the water.
